headline: FIREFLY METALS DRILLS 11.5m AT 13.2% CuEq — Green Bay PEA On Track For August; 65m Zone Confirmed (TSX/ASX: FFM)
snippet: FireFly Metals (TSX/ASX: FFM) released another batch of high-grade assays on August 3 from its six-rig underground drill program at the Green Bay Copper-Gold VMS Project in Newfoundland, including 11.5 metres at 13.2% CuEq (11.1% Cu, 2.1 g/t Au), 18.9m at 8.2% CuEq, and 65.3m at 4.3% CuEq — all feeding into an imminent resource update and Preliminary Economic Assessment on track for completion by end of August. The current resource stands at 50.4 Mt at 2.0% CuEq M&I with a high-grade Core Zone of 8.8 Mt at 3.9% CuEq; infill drilling is targeting at least 70% M&I classification before a maiden Ore Reserve is declared before year-end. For copper investors watching a near-term PEA catalyst at current prices above US$6.40/lb, the August timing window is shrinking.

headline: GOLD $4,069 / SILVER $58 AS US PAUSES IRAN AIRSTRIKES — Softer Dollar Supports; NFP Friday Is The Swing Vote
snippet: Gold futures opened at $4,135/oz and spot held near $4,069 while silver climbed to $58.26 on Monday August 3 after President Trump announced the US would pause planned airstrikes against Iran — pushing oil prices sharply lower and reducing near-term inflation fears. A softer US dollar added support, with Kitco noting the metals are firmer but range-bound ahead of Friday's nonfarm payrolls report, which will either cement or reprice the two-thirds probability of a September Federal Reserve rate hike. Iran's leaders publicly denied active negotiations with the US (saying talks are only with Oman regarding the Strait of Hormuz), adding uncertainty, but the de-escalation was enough to lift gold off Friday's lows.

headline: KAZATOMPROM H1 2026 URANIUM OUTPUT SURGES 9% — 13,291 Tonnes Produced; Kazakhstan Holds 38% Of Global Supply
snippet: Kazatomprom, the world's largest uranium producer, reported on August 3 that Kazakhstan's H1 2026 uranium production reached 13,291 tonnes of U3O8 equivalent — a 9% year-on-year increase from 12,242 tonnes in H1 2025 — as the state-run operator's 26 deposits across 14 asset clusters ran at full capacity in line with its full-year 2026 guidance of 71.5 to 75.4 million pounds of U3O8. The output growth arrives as spot uranium holds near $85-86/lb. Kazakhstan accounts for approximately 38% of global uranium supply, making Kazatomprom's production trajectory the single most important supply-side variable for Western uranium developers and explorers watching whether the anticipated utility re-contracting cycle translates into sustained term price appreciation.

headline: INDONESIA UNBLOCKS RARE EARTH EXPORT CHAOS — Bauxite, Copper, Nickel Shipments Clear; 85 Surveys Released
snippet: Indonesia resumed exports of minerals including bauxite, alumina, copper cathodes, and nickel derivatives on August 3, 2026 after Presidential Chief of Staff Dudung Abdurachman clarified that the national rare earth export ban does NOT apply to REE content found as incidental byproducts in primary mining commodities — ending weeks of shipment delays caused by mandatory REE content inspections. The unblocking released 85 previously stalled surveyors' reports through state firm PT Sucofindo. The episode illustrates the cascading regulatory friction that China's REE export controls have set off globally: even unintended secondary effects of REE regulations can freeze supply chains for unrelated commodities like copper cathodes and nickel.

headline: FED'S HAWKISH 9-3 HOLD PUTS SEPTEMBER HIKE AT 67% — Metals Range-Bound; NFP Friday Looms
snippet: Kitco's August 3 AM report identifies the key tension suppressing precious metals: the Federal Reserve's July 30 decision to hold rates at 3.50-3.75% came in a 9-3 vote with three dissenters pushing for an immediate hike — leaving markets pricing a two-thirds probability of a September rate hike. Gold at $4,047-$4,069 and silver at $57.57-$58.26 are range-bound as traders position ahead of Friday's nonfarm payrolls print. A strong jobs number confirms the September hike and represents a headwind for metals; a miss reprices the probability lower and opens upside. For junior mining investors, the 9-3 vote structure is more hawkish than the single policy rate implies — any NFP surprise is amplified by the existing internal dissent.

headline: SMARTKEM ACQUIRES FERROX CRITICAL MINERALS — $125M All-Stock Deal Builds Titanium, Vanadium, Iron Platform On Nasdaq
snippet: SmartKem, Inc. (Nasdaq) announced August 3, 2026 that it will acquire Ferrox Critical Minerals Ltd. in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately US$125 million, combining SmartKem's materials science platform with Ferrox's Tivani titanium-iron-vanadium mining assets to create a long-life critical minerals platform. The deal is subject to shareholder, regulatory, and Nasdaq approvals with a March 31, 2027 deadline. For junior mining investors, the transaction is a data point on the growing M&A appetite for non-precious, non-copper critical minerals outside the battery metals category — specifically titanium and vanadium, which receive limited coverage despite their defense and clean energy applications.

headline: SSR MINING SOARS ON Q2 BEAT — Mid-Tier Gold Producer Tops Expectations; Stock Rallies After-Market (Nasdaq/TSX: SSRM)
snippet: SSR Mining Inc. (Nasdaq/TSX: SSRM) released Q2 2026 financial results after market close on August 4, with Mining.com reporting the stock 'soared' on a 'significant beat' versus analyst expectations. SSR Mining is a free-cash-flow-focused gold and silver producer with operations across the Americas, tracking toward its full-year 2026 production guidance of 450,000-535,000 gold equivalent ounces. At gold averaging above $4,400/oz in Q2, a beat at the production and cost level carries meaningful free cash flow implications — and at current $4,069/oz spot, SSRM's operating leverage to $4,000+ gold makes Q2 results relevant for investors benchmarking mid-tier producer valuations against the gold price.
